Order No.07/ Dated:18.01.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Mahila P.S. Case No. 07 of 2022 instituted under Sections 323/ 498A/ 504/ 506 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act 1961, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case in order to extort money from the petitioner.
The allegations are false, fabricated, general and omnibus in nature.
Real fact is that informant does not want to reside with the petitioner and asking heavy amount of levy for settlement of the case which is beyond the reach of the petitioner.
Petitioner is a qualified person and after post graduation in management is working in medical store.

The informant is a short tempered lady and always used to quarrel with the petitioner and family members, hence, complaint case no. 401 of 2022 (annexure 2) was lodged by the petitioner against the informant and her family member.
Petitioner has no criminal antecedent.

It is lastly submitted that the petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the investigation of the case and also abide by all terms and conditions which may be imposed in the matter of granting anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Learned Addl.P.P assisted with learned counsel for the informant appearing for the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner and submitted that marriage of the informant was solemnized on 05.11.2020 and Rs. 20,000,00/- was spent on jewelleries, clothes, furniture and other house old articles given in present.
Rs. 3,50,000/- were also deposited in the bank account of the petitioner elder brother, Dr. Jiyaul Haq and mother of the petitioner, Sanjida Khatun.

On demand from mother and elder brother of the petitioner Rs. 3,50,000/- lacs was deposited in the name of informant and she joined matrimonial home after marriage but on the same night her Md. The informant told that her father had already spent Rs. 25, 000,00/- in the said marriage but he could not fulfil the further demand,
thereafter, her husband started assaulting her and frequently used to quarrel and have consumed poison.
It is also alleged that due to torture informant fell ill but no medical facility was provided to her.
Hence, she informed to her father who brought her at parental home on 23.03.2021.

She is still taunted and tormented and subjected to mental cruelty by her husband and other family members,
who has lodged false cases against the informant and her family members in order to pressurize them to withdraw this case and are inclined towards their own terms and conditions.
Learned counsel for the informant has filed an exhibit A copy of the complaint case lodged by the petitioner just after receiving notice in this case from the police station.

Case lodged by the elder brother of the informant namely, Jiyaul Haq Ansari in Meral P.S. Case No. 82 of 2022 against the family members of the informant but informant has also filed a list of articles including the jewelleries presented at the time of marriage.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and rival contentions of the learned counsel, I found that there are serious allegations against the petitioner that the informant is also being subjected to cruelty by lodging criminal cases against the family members just after institution of this case.

Considering the rival submission of learned counsels and materials available against petitioner as well as gravity of allegations, I am not inclined to grant privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner, which stands rejected.
Petitioner is directed to surrender before the court below and pray for regular bail, the learned court below shall consider the same on its own merits, without being prejudiced by this order.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) R.K/A.P.K.
